summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a Professor at Vidyasagar College and in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta, and he taught Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (~1993–1999) and held posts at Leipzig University and Heidelberg University, teaching Florin Deleanu and David Fiordalis.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director at Quaid-i-Azam University, Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums of Andhra Pradesh, and Deputy Director at the Taxila Museum.
Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University (~1925–1929), later served as its president (~1949–1978), and taught Chung-yuan Chang.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982), earned a BA at Komazawa University (~1986–1990), and completed an MA under Roderick S. Bucknell at the University of Queensland (~1991–1998).

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral course at Tohoku University (~1986–1991), later serving as an assistant professor at Iwate University (~1996–2004) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~2004).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1973) and Harvard University (~1974–1979). He served as an assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1979–1989) and as a professor at Kyoto University (~1989–2009).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh works in Tibetology, religious studies, and other fields. She completed her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (~2005–2010).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Dalhousie University, Balliol College, and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton, later serving as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from 1940.

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya and Harvard universities, and held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, SOKENDAI, the University of Hamburg, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (b. 1947) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, holding posts at JNU, University of Chicago, UW–Madison, Leiden University, Collège de France, and EHESS.

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at University College Dublin (~1917–1922), he held posts at UCD (~1930–1937), University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1946), the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1949–1972), and Trinity College Dublin.
Myoshin Fujitake (b. 1956) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a committee post at the Otani Society until 2000 and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1940), and as a professor at the University of Mysore (~1916–1927).

Mónika Kiss works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied as a doctoral student of Japanese studies at Eötvös Loránd University, where she was advised by Masanori Yamaji and taught by Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (~1940–1952) and later as a professor at Visva-Bharati University (~1952–1964).

N. Veezhinathan is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras (~1931–1946) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums (~1961–1970).
Nagin J. Shah (b. 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology in 1968, succeeding Dalsukh D. Malvania, and he taught Maria Heim.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chittagong College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London, later serving as Head of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta until ~1958.
